newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Police put Sri Lanka MP, ex-mayor on wanted list.
newsitem.headline: Police put Sri Lanka MP, ex-mayor on wanted list.

text.p: Sri Lankan police on Thursday offered a reward for the arrest of a lawmaker and a former mayor from the main opposition United National Party (UNP) wanted as suspects in the killing of a ruling coalition politician.

A statement by the Inspector-General of Police said a reward of one million rupees ($17,500) would be paid to anyone providing information leading to the arrest of the UNP lawmaker, Susantha Punchinilame, and Mahinda Ratnatilleke, former UNP mayor of Ratnapura city.

Nalanda Ellawala, 29, a member of parliament from Sri Lanka's ruling People's Alliance, was gunned down in Ratnapura district south of Colombo on Tuesday during a roadside quarrel between his supporters and rivals from the UNP.

"Police are soliciting the cooperation from the public to provide information regarding the hideouts of...Punchinilame or Ratnatilleke...who are wanted for the assassination of Nalanda Ellawala," the police bulletin said.
The statement described the two as suspects.
The killing occurred on the eve of the deadline for filing nominations for local polls on March 21, the first electoral test for President Chandrika Kumaratunga's coalition government.
Her alliance toppled the UNP from 17 years in power in 1994.

The polls are for local assemblies and mayors in seven of the country's nine provinces. The government scrapped polls in the northern and eastern provinces because of guerrilla activity by separatist Tamils.
Earlier in the day, UNP leader and former prime minister Ranil Wickremesinghe said the two suspects should report to police.
Wickremesinghe said he had telephoned Punchinilame soon after the incident and told him to seek the advice of lawyers. He said he had had no contact with him since.
"Any UNP member found guilty in this incident will be expelled from the party," Wickremesinghe told a news conference.
"We condemn these killings," he said. "Let the guilty be punished. There's been too much violence in this country. The UNP has denounced the culture of political violence."
Wickremesinghe said UNP supporters in Ratnapura had been attacked and several homes and shops set on fire by mobs after the killing.
"We're going to face this election come what may, whatever the conditions, and we'll win," Wickremesinghe said.
